newsitem.title: GERMANY: Cohen opens door for compromise on NATO command.
newsitem.headline: Cohen opens door for compromise on NATO command.

text.p: Responding to a German initiative, the United States on Tuesday opened the door to the possibility of giving up or sharing the command of southern NATO forces with a European officer after a delay of perhaps five years.

"We have a completely open mind," U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen told reporters after German Defence Minister Volker Ruehe announced a tentative proposal to delay a fight between the United States and France over the command issue for five or six years.

Ruehe said during a joint news conference with visiting Cohen that German, French, British, Spanish and Italian officials met on Tuesday to try and develop a European position on France's demand that Washington give up its traditional command of NATO's Southern Forces in Naples. U.S. sources said the meeting was in Bonn.

The United States had until now flatly refused to surrender the command to a European officer and Ruehe suggested a consensus was emerging in Europe to leave the command in U.S. hands now but reconsider the issue in five or six years while strengthening European participation in the region.
Cohen said in response to questions that the United States was willing to review the matter in five, six or seven years, but stressed that the command might still remain in U.S. hands.

"When we say we would like to review, or plan to review, the situation in a number of years, we have a completely open mind," he said. "And there are several possible outcomes: number one it (the command) will remain with the United States, number two it could rotate between the Europeans and the United States, and third, it could rotate among the Europeans."
